conviction_note: No not-yet-public company number was found and no Q3 consensus could be sourced. The findings net to 0.0: Aker-linked insider buying and organisational cuts that keep the synergy plan on track offset the merger one-off costs, the risk of a reset under an acting CEO and slower 2027 rents. The scaled number is p_up 47 on an abs_move of 5.5, giving -0.33. The move is wide because this is the first combined report after the KlaraBo merger and it carries a new earnings capacity. p_up sits just under 50 because the name missed the property-management-result bar in Q1 and Q2 2026 and was sold both times (-2.58%, -5.22%), and that is a reaction history, not a sourced Q3 number.

already_public.what: Merger with KlaraBo completed and registered 30 Sep 2026; 85,496,012 B and 20,004,545 A shares issued as consideration (Q3 balance sheet consolidates KlaraBo and the SBB portfolio at quarter-end)
CEO Erik Hävermark removed with immediate effect, board member Sophia Mattsson-Linnala acting CEO, recruitment 6-9 months
Organisational review: ~50 positions redundant, headcount ~270 -> ~220, two regions, COO role removed

Synergy targets: >= SEK 120m a year (85m operational within 12 months, 35m financial as debt is refinanced); standalone earnings capacity at 30 Jun 2026 SEK 477m = 2.42 SEK/share; long-term NAV 81.80 SEK/share
No profit warning (vinstvarning) or pre-release of Q3 in the Nasdaq Nordic feed through 2026-11-17

new_in_release.expect: The first combined earnings capacity (intjäningsförmåga) per share after the merger. The bar is the parties' pro forma of about 2.75 SEK/share including synergies (Affärsvärlden, snippet only). Direction unknown: the new organisation supports the synergy plan, but an acting CEO may reset assumptions.

Q3 property management result, Svea standalone in the P&L because the merger closed on the last day of the quarter. Q3 is seasonally stronger than Q2 (110m), but merger one-off costs (~SEK 55m in total, timing unknown) may land in it. Two misses in a row against Modular consensus. Slight negative lean, low confidence.

Merger accounting. Shares were issued at ~31 SEK against a long-term NAV of ~81 SEK/share, so a large non-cash gain (bargain purchase or revaluation) is likely in Q3 net profit. Headline noise; NAV per share should be roughly unchanged.
unknown: the combined company was pitched on stronger dividend capacity, and a policy statement is possible but not signalled
Q3 property value change: peers' Q3 2026 residential revaluations were small positives, so expect a small positive

findings.finding: The merger was estimated to carry about SEK 55m of one-off costs. The Q3 report covers the quarter in which the merger closed (30 Sep), so part of that likely lands in Q3 central administration or a separate line, and redundancy costs for ~50 roles follow in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 missed the 123m consensus (110m), partly on elevated admin costs (variable pay), and the stock fell 5.22% on 2026-07-16.
findings.original_quote: Bolagen räknar med att spara minst 120 miljoner kronor per år ... Fusionen beräknas samtidigt kosta runt 55 miljoner kronor i engångskostnader. (The companies expect to save at least SEK 120m a year ... The merger is at the same time expected to cost around SEK 55m in one-off costs.)
findings.why_not_priced: Whether the costs sit inside the property management result, which is the line the Modular consensus is built on, is not public. If analysts exclude them and the company includes them, the headline reads as a miss, as it did in Q2. Small because it is a one-off with no path to the earnings capacity.
findings.independence: The Q2 admin-cost overrun and the CEO's comment that admin costs fluctuate between quarters: https://www.placera.se/telegram/sveafastigheter-ska-uppna-synergier-med-klarabo-pa-12-man-vd-20260716

findings.finding: The CEO was removed with immediate effect 14 days after the merger closed, with no reason given. The Q3 report is the first under acting CEO Mattsson-Linnala, appointed by a chairman (Lennart Sten, also SBB chair) who replaced the SBB CEO the same way in August. A first report under new leadership carries a raised risk of reset assumptions: earnings capacity, project and building-rights values (SEK 3.6bn non-income-generating at Q1).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior leadership-change print for this name. The stock fell 2.1% and 1.5% on 8 and 12 Oct and rose 2.5% the day after the 14 Oct CEO announcement.
findings.original_quote: Bostadsbolaget Sveafastigheter gör som storägaren SBB och byter vd på dagen. (The residential company Sveafastigheter does as its major owner SBB did and replaces its CEO with immediate effect.)
findings.why_not_priced: The removal is public. What it means for the numbers is not. No write-down or revision has been filed (the Nasdaq Nordic feed has no inside-information item since 18 May). A reset would be visible as a lower earnings-capacity figure or negative project revaluations on the day. Sized small because this is inference from a public event, not a document.
findings.independence: The organisational review of 27 Oct already revised the management structure announced on 15 Oct, which shows the new leadership is changing plans quickly: https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b91c6e50b2f2494019a5e85bbc10020f9&lang=en&src=listed

findings.finding: Within four weeks of closing, the combined company identified ~50 redundant positions (organisation ~270 -> ~220 including consultants), roughly half of the SEK 85m operational synergy target at a typical SEK 0.8-1.0m fully loaded cost per role. That supports the first combined earnings capacity coming in at or near the parties' synergy case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock moved -0.49% on 27 Oct, the day of the announcement.
findings.original_quote: Den preliminära bedömningen är att övertaligheten omfattar cirka 50 tjänster ... syftar till att förenkla organisationen, tydliggöra ansvaret för förvaltningen och realisera de synergier som kommunicerades i samband med fusionen. (The preliminary assessment is that about 50 positions are redundant ... aims to simplify the organisation ... and realise the synergies communicated in connection with the merger.)
findings.why_not_priced: The headcount is public. How it converts into the earnings capacity per share is not, and the market's reaction on 27 Oct was flat. If it were priced as delivering the 2.75 SEK/share case, the stock would trade above the 11.5x P/FR it holds at 31.5. Net of the rest of the company, it is one input to a figure that also absorbs lost SBB management fees (54m income / 47m cost in the standalone earnings capacity).
findings.independence: The 85m operational / 35m financial split and the 12-month timeline: https://www.placera.se/telegram/sveafastigheter-ska-uppna-synergier-med-klarabo-pa-12-man-vd-20260716

findings.finding: Merger consideration was paid in shares issued at ~31-33 SEK while the exchange ratio was set on long-term NAV (Svea 81.40 SEK/share). The Q3 accounts therefore likely carry a multi-billion-SEK non-cash gain (bargain purchase or revaluation of acquired properties). SBB postponed its own Q3 report to 24 Nov specifically to analyse the transaction's accounting implications.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for this name. Swedish property stocks trade on the property management result and NAV, not net profit.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side will look through it. It could produce a wire headline of a large profit on a 3-analyst, $0.9m/day name with retail holders, but a one-off with no path to the guide is sold or ignored, so it is held near 0. The treatment is unknown and could also go the other way, through how acquired properties are marked.
findings.independence: The long-term NAV basis and 81.40 SEK/share: https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=bc4a604d4167ac533caadfa3c71da7817&lang=en&src=listed (exchange ratio based on long-term NAV)

findings.finding: 2027 Swedish residential rent settlements are landing around 2.5-3% (arbiters average 2.8%; West Sweden 2.60-2.90%), while Stockholm's municipal companies ask 4.31%. That points to slower like-for-like rental growth in any 2027 outlook the combined company gives.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No company-specific record. This is sector-wide news.
findings.original_quote: Hyrorna höjs med 3 procent – båda sidor rasar (Rents raised by 3 percent – both sides furious)
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced, because it is a sector-wide public series. It is filed because the release may state its own 2027 rent outcome, the transmission to this company is not yet confirmed, and it is sized small.

findings.finding: Residential peers that reported Q3 2026 showed small positive unrealised value changes (Wallenstam +107m, Heba +99.9m). That points to a small positive Q3 revaluation for Sveafastigheter and no NAV shock from the market side.

baseline_tension: There is no real lean to cut against: priced_lean_pct -0.04, run-up +0.86% over 20 days, short register at the truncation floor. The findings net to zero, and the slight negative p_up comes from the reaction history of two missed and sold prints, not from a sourced Q3 number.
language_note: The Swedish FI insider register (marknadssok.fi.se) carried the Aker-linked purchases of 8.1m B shares at 30.20-32.25 between 30 Sep and 16 Oct, which no English wire item covered

The Swedish press (Realtid, EFN) carried the ~SEK 55m one-off merger cost estimate and the framing that the CEO was removed 'på dagen' the same way SBB's was, with the chairman's 6-9 month recruitment guess; the English company release gave no reason and no timeline

The Nyhetsbyrån Direkt interview (Swedish) carried the split of the 120m synergies into 85m operational within 12 months and 35m financial, and the cause of the Q2 admin overrun (variable pay for 2025)
The company releases themselves were identical in English and Swedish: nothing in the filings is Swedish-only
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' / size on what is new: the first combined earnings capacity is a guidance-scale line and the period is not pre-released, so abs_move_pct went from 4.5 to 5.5 (the history median of 2.94 is a lower bound)
'A beat made of a one-off is sold': the accounting-gain finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1

'Two findings resting on one document are one finding': the redundancy-cost and synergy-delivery items both rested on the 27 Oct release, so they were merged (+0.4 became +0.3 net), and the one-off cost finding now rests only on the 55m merger-cost estimate (-0.4 became -0.3)
'Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis' / own caveat: the CEO-reset inference was trimmed from -0.5 to -0.4
Reaction history moves p_up, not size: p_up held at 47 for the two sold misses, and abs_move_pct was not capped by them
